groups.title: Section A · 第 1 篇 · 1–4 题
groups.material:
M: I've just bought a new blender.
W: What's that?
M: A blender, you know, a machine that blends food.
W: Uh, yes, of course, the electric kitchen appliance.
M: Exactly, this one is state-of-the-art. I've been meaning to buy one for a while, and I did thorough research on which specific model to get. I read through maybe hundreds of online user reviews. Anyway, it's amazing.
W: Really? What could be so special about it? I mean it's just a blender.
M: Well, basically, it's just a very good one. It feels heavy and sturdy and well made. It also has lots of power and can easily cut and crush practically anything. This way, the soups and juices I make come out really fine and smooth, with no lumpy bits.
W: Um, I see. I've never thought of getting one myself. It sounds like the kind of thing that, for me personally, I would rarely use.
M: I've never had one before, and now that I do. I use it all the time. I make a fresh fruit juice in the morning, maybe not every morning, but three or four times a week, and it feels fantastic. It's a really healthy habit.
W: I can imagine that must feel quite satisfying. I can picture you getting all creative in the kitchen and trying out a multitude of different ingredient combinations, and it's obviously going to be healthier than buying packaged juice from a supermarket.
M: It's so much healthier. It's not even close. Did you know that store-bought juice is like 10% sugar?
W: Right, so then you bought it for the health benefits?
M: Mostly yes. Basically, it allows me to have a more varied diet with a far wider assortment of nutrients, because it's not only fruit in my morning juices you see. I can also throw in vegetables, nuts, yogurts, cereals, anything that tickles my fancy.

groups.title: Section A · 第 2 篇 · 5–8 题
groups.material:
W: Today we have a very interesting guest. Mr. Thomas Benjamin Grimm, the mayor of Berkton, is here to talk about his job and responsibilities overseeing this charming village. Mr. Grimm, thank you for being here.
M: Thank you for having me.
W: I'd like to start by stating the obvious. Berkton has become one of the most popular tourist destinations in the country, and this has happened under your watch. Just how did you achieve this?
M: The achievement belongs to all the residents of Berkton. It was a shared effort where everybody pitched in for the communal good.
W: But how did this change happen? In about 10 years, Berkton has gone from a relatively unheard-of sleepy village to a must-see destination.
M: Yes, the change has truly been remarkable. Berkton was always fortunate to be endowed with such a beautiful natural allure. The Ambury Hills above the village remain untouched by human development, and the Sonora Valley just below it is equally stunning. The transformation commenced in a town hall meeting in spring 2008 over 10 years ago now, when an overwhelming majority of neighbors voted in favor of "Motion 836". This legislative proposal essentially set out to harmonize the aesthetic appearance of all the houses in Berkton. The idea was that if all the properties looked a certain way with shared design features, then a village as a whole would look more beautiful. And it worked.
W: It certainly did. I'm looking now at a before-and-after photo, and the change is truly remarkable. It's hard to believe it's the same place. And how do the neighbors feel now?
M: Great pride, I would say.
W: But what about the multitudes of visitors now crowding the streets? Is everyone happy about that?
M: The tourists we receive are a blessing, as they have completely revitalized our local economy. Every visitor is warmly welcome.

groups.title: Section B · 第 1 篇 · 9–11 题
groups.material:
Researchers in the US have created a remote-controlled robot that is so small it can walk on the top of a US penny. In research published in the journal Science Robotics, a team at Northwestern University said the crab-like robot is 0.5mm wide. Researchers described it as the smallest-ever remote-controlled walking robot.
The tiny robot can bend, twist, crawl, walk, turn, and even jump without the use of complex hardware or special power. The engineers said this is because the robot is powered by the elastic property of its body. To construct the robot, the researchers used a shape-memory alloy material that transforms to its remembered shape when heated.
Using a laser, the team is able to heat the robot at specific parts of its body, causing it to change shape. As the robot deforms and goes back to its original shape, it creates movement from one place to another. "Because these structures are so tiny, the rate of cooling is very fast," project lead Professor John A. Rogers said. "In fact, reducing the sizes of these robots allows them to run faster."
While the research is still in the exploratory phase, the team believes that technology could lead to micro-sized robots that can perform practical tasks in tightly confined spaces. "You might imagine micro-robots as agents to repair or assemble small structures or machines in industry or as surgical assistants to clear clogged arteries, to stop internal bleeding, or to eliminate cancerous tumours—all in minimally invasive procedures," Rogers said.

groups.title: Section B · 第 2 篇 · 12–15 题
groups.material:
I don't want to boast or anything, but I have always considered myself something of an elite sleeper. Given the opportunity, I will sleep for marathon stretches, and can doze through the most extreme situations. On one very rough ferry crossing, on the route to the Isles of Scilly, for example, my traveling companion spent the entire 3-hour-ride throwing up in the bathroom, while I dozed happily on a plastic chair.
Unfortunately, it has come to my attention that I am not an elite sleeper after all. It seems I am just lazy, because elite sleepers are defined as the approximately 3 percent of the population who are biologically programmed to need less sleep than the rest of us. According to a study that came out in March, elite sleepers have rare genetic changes, which means they can sleep fewer hours than mere mortals, without any risk of cognitive decline.
It may not be possible to change your own genes, but can you train yourself to need less sleep? Is there a non-biological way to reach elite sleeper status? I have spent the past year trying to answer that question. Not for fun, I should add, but because having a baby has severely disrupted my sleep, for which I still have a great passion.
For a while, I assumed I'd be forced to become one of those people who jump out of bed at the crack of dawn. After a year of tough scientific study, however, I have discovered being forced to get up early in the morning is very different from being an early bird.

groups.title: Section C · 第 1 篇 · 16–18 题
groups.material:
If you read an article about a controversial issue, do you think you'd realise if it had changed your beliefs? No one knows your own mind like you do—it seems obvious that you would know if your beliefs had shifted. And yet a new paper in the Quarterly Journal of Experimental Psychology suggests that we actually have very poor awareness of our own belief change, meaning that we will tend to underestimate how much we've been swayed by a convincing article.
The researchers recruited over two hundred undergraduates across two studies and focused on their beliefs about whether physical punishment of kids is an effective form of discipline. The students reported their initial beliefs about whether physical punishment is an effective way to discipline a child on a scale from "1" completely disbelieve to "9" completely believe. Several weeks later they were given one of two research-based texts to read: each was several pages long and either presented the arguments and data in favour of physical punishment or against it. After this, the students answered some questions to test their comprehension and memory of the text. Then, the students again scored their belief about whether physical punishment is effective or not. Finally, the researchers asked them to recall what their belief had been at the start of the study.
The students' belief about physical punishment changed when they read a text that argued against their own initial position. Crucially, the memory of their initial belief was shifted in the direction of their new belief—in fact, their memory was closer to their current belief than their original belief. The more their belief had changed, the larger this memory bias tended to be, suggesting the students were relying on their current belief to deduce the initial belief. The memory bias was unrelated to the measures of how well they'd understood or recalled the text, suggesting these factors didn't play a role in memory of initial belief or awareness of belief change.
The researchers concede that this research was about changes to mostly moderate beliefs—it's likely the findings would be different in the context of changes to extreme or deeply held beliefs. However, our beliefs on most topics are in the moderate range, and as we go about our daily lives reading informative material, these intriguing findings suggest we are mostly ignorant of how what we just read has updated and altered our own position.

groups.title: Section C · 第 2 篇 · 19–21 题
groups.material:
As the American population grows, so does the number of American moms. But, more than a century after Mother's Day became an official holiday, even as that number increases, the share of the American population who are mothers is at the lowest point in a quarter century.
It's frequently noted that fertility rates are falling sharply in richer countries. But the less-observed consequence of this trend is that the decline in births can also mean a decline in motherhood in America. According to my analysis of data from the Census Bureau, the decline of American motherhood is real, occurring very quickly, and may continue for some time yet.
Not only are moms making up less of the population, but their characteristics are changing too, and in a way that might be linked to their proportional decline. Moms today tend to be older than in the past. Just looking at recent years, the change in age-specific birth rates has been drastic.
In just the past few years, the peak childbearing age range for American women has advanced from that of 25-29 to that of 30-34. Meanwhile, childbearing among women under 20 has fallen by half or more, while childbearing among women 35 and older is rising.
One positive consequence of this age shift is that a larger proportion of new mothers are economically prepared to raise children. Less positively, however, many women find that, as they age, they can't have as many kids as they would like. Plus, having children later in life can increase the risk of health complications. These finer points aside, one major consequence of the older-moms trend is that fewer years of a woman's life are spent as a mother. This means that, at any given time, a larger share of women, and thus of the whole population, will report not having children in government surveys. In other words, later motherhood means less motherhood.
Even as motherhood rates decline, Mother's Day, of course, will endure. In fact, despite the demographic shift, retail spending on the holiday appears to be rising. It is hard to say if Mother's Day spending is rising more than one would expect, given that the American population keeps growing, but one factor might be that the proportion of women who are the mothers of adult children is rising. And those adult children may spend more generously when it comes to celebrating the moms they no longer live with.

groups.title: Section C · 第 3 篇 · 22–25 题
groups.material:
Since NASA published a paper in 1989 claiming that houseplants can soak up pollution and toxic chemicals, businesses and homeowners have increasingly invested in greenery to help clean their air. But, a new analysis suggests it could actually take more than 1,000 plants per square meter to gain a benefit any greater than simply opening a couple of windows.
The problem lies in the fact that NASA conducted their tests in sealed containers that do not simulate the conditions in most people's homes or offices. The space agency was primarily concerned about keeping the air fresh for astronauts cut off in biospheres or space stations and helping to combat "sick building syndrome", which had become a problem due to the super insulated and energy efficient offices of the late 1970s. By the early 1980s, workers regularly complained of skin rashes, sleeplessness, headaches, and allergies as they breathed in toxic chemicals from paints and plastics.
NASA found that certain plants could remove chemicals from the air, and even today, garden centers recommend the plants for air cleaning properties. However, a new evaluation of dozens of studies spanning 30 years found that houseplants in a normal environment have little impact. In fact, natural ventilation is far better at cleaning the air. The researchers also calculated the clean air delivery rate for plants in the studies they analyzed and found that the rate at which plants disperse the compounds was well below the usual rate of air exchange in a normal building, caused by the movement of people coming and going, opening doors and windows.
Many of the studies did show a reduction in the concentration of volatile organic compounds over time, which is likely why people have seized on them to praise the air purifying virtues of plants. But the researchers' calculation showed it would take 10 to 1,000 plants per square meter of floor space to compete with the air cleaning capacity of a building's air handling system or even just a couple of open windows in a house. In contrast, NASA's sealed experiment recommended one pot plant per 100 square feet.
This is certainly an example of how scientific findings can be misleading or misinterpreted over time. But it's also a great example of how scientific research should continually reexamine and question findings to get closer to the ground truth of understanding what's actually happening.

questions.prompt: What does the man say he did before buying the blender?
options: Read numerous comments users put online.
Blended all his food without using a machine.
Searched for the state-of-the-art models of blenders.
Did thorough research on the price of kitchen appliances.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the man say he did before buying the blender? 

 【翻译】 男士说他在购买搅拌机之前做了什么？ 
 A)  阅读了大量用户在网上发布的评论。 
 B)  不使用机器搅拌他所有的食物。 
 C)  搜索了最先进的搅拌机型号。 
 D)  对厨房电器的价格做了彻底的研究。 

 【答案】 A （细节题） Read numerous comments users put online. 
 【定位】 P5 I did thorough research on which specific model to get. I read through maybe hundreds of online user reviews. 
 我对具体该买哪个型号做了彻底的研究。我大概读了几百条网上的用户评论。 

 【信号】 男方自述买前动作 。这题问"the man...did before buying"，信号就是男方在介绍这台机器时，自己说出的那串"我做了……"。关键落点是 I read through maybe hundreds of online user reviews，"读了几百条网上用户评论"正是买前的准备动作。 

 【替换】 read through maybe hundreds of online user reviews ↔ Read numerous comments users put online. 几百条=numerous，评论=comments 

 【排除】 C) 原词陷阱 录音里 state-of-the-art 是男方用来夸"这台机器很先进"（this one is state-of-the-art），并不是说他"去搜寻顶配机型"。选项 Searched for the state-of-the-art models of blenders. 把这个原词搬过来拼成一个他没做的动作，听到 state-of-the-art 就选就中招。  借用原文：this one is state-of-the-art 

 D) 偷换概念 男方确实说了 I did thorough research，但研究的是 which specific model to get（该买哪个型号），不是价格。选项 Did thorough research on the price of kitchen appliances. 偷偷把研究对象换成 price，听到"thorough research"就选就被偷换。  借用原文：I did thorough research on which specific model to get 

 B) 与原文相反 选项 Blended all his food without using a machine. 说"不用机器就把食物搅了"，可整段重点恰恰是他买了一台机器（blender 就是机器）。这和录音说的正相反，属无中生有又反向的陷阱。

questions.prompt: What does the woman say she has never thought of doing?
options: Eating any blended food.
Buying a blender herself.
Using machines to do her cooking.
Making soups and juices for herself.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the woman say she has never thought of doing? 

 【翻译】 女士说她从未想过做什么？ 
 A)  吃任何搅拌食品。 
 B)  自己购买一台搅拌机。 
 C)  使用机器来做饭。 
 D)  自己制作汤和果汁。 

 【答案】 B （细节题） Buying a blender herself. 
 【定位】 P8 I've never thought of getting one myself. 
 我自己从没想过要买一台。 

 【信号】 女方应答中的never thought原话 。题干问 never thought of doing，录音里女方原话就是 I've never thought of getting one myself，"never thought of"与题干几乎一字不差，这句被问者的直接应答就是答案句。one 指上文的 blender。 

 【替换】 never thought of getting one myself ↔ Buying a blender herself. getting one=buying a blender，myself=herself 

 【排除】 D) 张冠李戴 soups and juices 是男方说的（他做的汤和果汁 the soups and juices I make），不是女方"从没想过给自己做"的事。选项 Making soups and juices for herself. 把男方做的事安到女方头上，是张冠李戴。  借用原文：the soups and juices I make 

 C) 原词陷阱 录音里 machine 出现在介绍 blender 时（a machine that blends food），女方并没说自己"从没想过用机器做饭"。选项 Using machines to do her cooking. 借 machine 这个原词编了个她没表过的态。  借用原文：a machine that blends food 

 A) 未提及 选项 Eating any blended food. 蹭了 blend 这个话题词，但女方从没说"从没想过吃任何搅拌食物"，她说的是没想过"买机器"。属未提及。

questions.prompt: What does the man say is a really healthy habit?
options: Cooking every meal creatively in the kitchen.
Paying due attention to his personal hygiene.
Eating breakfast punctually every morning.
Making his own fresh fruit juice regularly.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the man say is a really healthy habit? 

 【翻译】 男士说什么是真正健康的习惯？ 
 A)  在厨房里创意性地烹饪每一餐。 
 B)  适当关注他的个人卫生。 
 C)  每天早上准时吃早餐。 
 D)  定期自制新鲜果汁。 

 【答案】 D （细节题） Making his own fresh fruit juice regularly. 
 【定位】 P9 I make a fresh fruit juice in the morning, maybe not every morning, but three or four times a week, and it feels fantastic. It's a really healthy habit. 
 我早上会榨一杯鲜果汁，也许不是每天早上，而是一周三四次，感觉棒极了。这是个真正健康的习惯。 

 【信号】 healthy habit前紧挨的那件事 。答案信号是 It's a really healthy habit 里的 it——它回指紧挨着前面那件事 I make a fresh fruit juice in the morning...three or four times a week。男方把"经常自榨果汁"明确称作"真正健康的习惯"。 

 【替换】 I make a fresh fruit juice in the morning, maybe not every morning, but three or four times a week ↔ Making his own fresh fruit juice regularly. 一周三四次=regularly 

 【排除】 A) 与原文相反 Cooking every meal creatively in the kitchen. 借的 creative in the kitchen 是女方的猜想 getting all creative in the kitchen，不是男方说的健康习惯；而且 every meal（每一餐）比录音的"一周三四次"夸张得多，频率过头。  借用原文：getting all creative in the kitchen 

 C) 原词陷阱 录音男方只说早上榨果汁、还"不是每天早上"，Eating breakfast punctually every morning. 借 morning 这个原词，编出"每天准时吃早餐"，既无 breakfast 也无 punctually，是原词陷阱。  借用原文：I make a fresh fruit juice in the morning, maybe not every morning 

 B) 未提及 Paying due attention to his personal hygiene. 讲"个人卫生"，整段对话围绕果汁与营养，从没谈卫生，属未提及，靠跑题词凑数。

questions.prompt: What do we learn about store-bought juice from the conversation?
options: One-tenth of it is sugar.
It looks healthy and attractive.
One's fancy may be tickled by it.
It contains an assortment of nutrients.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What do we learn about store-bought juice from the conversation? 

 【翻译】 从对话中我们了解到关于商店购买的果汁的什么信息？ 
 A)  其中十分之一是糖。 
 B)  它看起来健康且有吸引力。 
 C)  它可能会引起人们的兴趣。 
 D)  它包含各种营养成分。 

 【答案】 A （细节题） One-tenth of it is sugar. 
 【定位】 P11 Did you know that store-bought juice is like 10% sugar? 
 你知道店里买的果汁差不多有百分之十是糖吗？ 

 【信号】 对象store-bought juice配数字 。题干对象 store-bought juice 在录音里只在 store-bought juice is like 10% sugar 这一句被正面描述，且带一个具体比例 10%。"对象点名 + 出现数字"双重信号，这句就是答案句。 

 【替换】 store-bought juice is like 10% sugar ↔ One-tenth of it is sugar. 10%=One-tenth 

 【排除】 D) 偷换概念 It contains an assortment of nutrients. 借的 assortment of nutrients 是男方夸"自榨晨间果汁"的（a far wider assortment of nutrients），对象是自榨果汁，不是店买果汁。题干问的是 store-bought，对象被偷换。  借用原文：a far wider assortment of nutrients 

 C) 原词陷阱 One's fancy may be tickled by it. 盗用 tickles my fancy，但录音里这词形容的是男方往自榨果汁里加 anything that tickles my fancy，和店买果汁无关，是张冠李戴的原词陷阱。  借用原文：anything that tickles my fancy 

 B) 与原文相反 It looks healthy and attractive. 蹭了 healthy 一词，但录音说"自榨"比店买更健康（It's so much healthier），从没说"店买果汁看起来健康诱人"，attractive 更是没提，属未提及兼相反。  借用原文：It's so much healthier

questions.prompt: What is the question the woman asked Mr. Grimm after the introduction?
options: How he has made himself popular as the mayor of Berkton.
How the residents will turn Berkton into a tourist attraction.
How charming he himself considers the village of Berkton to be.
How he has led people of Berkton to change the village radically.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What is the question the woman asked Mr. Grimm after the introduction? 

 【翻译】 这位女士在介绍之后向Grimm先生提出了什么问题? 
 A)  他如何使自己成为广受欢迎的Berkton市长。 
 B)  居民将如何把Berkton变成旅游胜地。 
 C)  他本人认为Berkton村有多迷人。 
 D)  他如何带领Berkton的人们彻底改变了这个村庄。 

 【答案】 D （细节题） How he has led people of Berkton to change the village radically. 
 【定位】 P3 Berkton has become one of the most popular tourist destinations in the country, and this has happened under your watch. Just how did you achieve this? 
 Berkton 已成为全国最受欢迎的旅游目的地之一，而这一切就发生在你的任期之内。你究竟是怎么做到这一点的呢？ 

 【信号】 主持人在介绍后抛出的直接提问句 。答案句的信号是主持人(W)在开场介绍之后说出的那句直接发问 Just how did you achieve this?——"this" 回指上一句 "Berkton 变成热门旅游地"，所以她问的正是 "你如何促成了这场转变"。对话题里，主持人 "介绍之后的第一个问句" 就是答案落点。 

 【替换】 how did you achieve this ↔ How he has led people of Berkton to change the village radically this＝把村子变旅游地，即 "彻底改变村庄" 
 this has happened under your watch ↔ he has led people of Berkton "在你任期内发生"＝市长带领大家做成 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 A 用了原文反复出现的 popular as the mayor of Berkton 这些原词，但主持人问的是 "如何改变村子"，不是 "市长本人如何变得受欢迎"；原文 popular tourist destinations 说的是 "村子" 受欢迎，A 偷换成 "市长" 受欢迎，听到 popular 就选会中招。  借用原文：Berkton has become one of the most popular tourist destinations in the country 

 B) 张冠李戴 B 说的是 the residents will turn Berkton into a tourist attraction，主语是居民、且是 "将要" 做的将来事；可主持人问的是 "你(市长)如何做到了已经发生的转变"，B 张冠李戴(把焦点从市长换成居民)又错了时态。  借用原文：The achievement belongs to all the residents of Berkton. 

 C) 原词陷阱 C 说 How charming he himself considers the village of Berkton to be，借用了原文 this charming village 里的 charming 一词；但 charming 是主持人介绍时用的，且主持人问的是 "如何做到转变"，不是 "市长觉得村子多迷人"，C 把客观描述偷换成 "市长的主观评价"。  借用原文：overseeing this charming village

questions.prompt: What do we learn about Berkton 10 years ago?
options: It was developed only to a limited extent.
It was totally isolated as a sleepy village.
It was relatively unknown to the outside.
It was endowed with rare natural resources.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What do we learn about Berkton 10 years ago? 

 【翻译】 关于10年前的Berkton我们了解到什么? 
 A)  它的开发程度很有限。 
 B)  它完全与世隔绝,是个沉睡的村庄。 
 C)  它在外界相对不为人知。 
 D)  它拥有稀有的自然资源。 

 【答案】 C （细节题） It was relatively unknown to the outside. 
 【定位】 P5 In about 10 years, Berkton has gone from a relatively unheard-of sleepy village to a must-see destination. 
 大约 10 年间，Berkton 从一个相对默默无闻的沉睡小村，变成了一个必看的旅游胜地。 

 【信号】 "from…to…" 中 from 后即 10 年前的状态 。答案信号是主持人这句 gone from a relatively unheard-of sleepy village to a must-see destination 里的 "from…to…" 结构：from 后面 a relatively unheard-of sleepy village 正是 "10 年前" 的起点状态，to 后面才是现在。问 "10 年前"，答案就在 from 之后。 

 【替换】 a relatively unheard-of sleepy village ↔ It was relatively unknown to the outside unheard-of＝unknown，同义替换 

 【排除】 A) 未提及 A 说 developed only to a limited extent(只在有限程度上被开发)，但原文只说村子 "没名气/沉睡"，从没说它 "被开发到有限程度"；这是凭 "沉睡村" 的印象自行脑补的开发说法，原文无据。 
 B) 原词陷阱 B 用了原文原词 sleepy village，但把 relatively unheard-of(相对没名气)夸大成 totally isolated(完全孤立)；relatively(相对)被偷换成 totally(完全)，程度被拔高，与原文不符。  借用原文：a relatively unheard-of sleepy village 

 D) 原词陷阱 D 说 endowed with rare natural resources，借用了原文 endowed with such a beautiful natural allure 的 endowed 与 natural；但原文说的是 "自然之美(allure)" 而非 "罕见资源(resources)"，且这句讲的不是 "10 年前的状态"，与题问的时间也不对。  借用原文：Berkton was always fortunate to be endowed with such a beautiful natural allure.

questions.prompt: What resulted from the passing of the legislative proposal "Motion 836"?
options: All the properties in Berkton were designed by the same architect.
The majority of residents lived in harmony with their neighbours.
The majority of residents enjoyed cosy housing conditions.
All the houses in Berkton looked aesthetically similar.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What resulted from the passing of the legislative proposal "Motion 836"? 

 【翻译】 立法提案"836号动议"的通过产生了什么结果? 
 A)  Berkton的所有房产都由同一位建筑师设计。 
 B)  大多数居民与邻居和睦相处。 
 C)  大多数居民享有舒适的住房条件。 
 D)  Berkton的所有房屋在美学上看起来相似。 

 【答案】 D （细节题） All the houses in Berkton looked aesthetically similar. 
 【定位】 P6 This legislative proposal essentially set out to harmonize the aesthetic appearance of all the houses in Berkton. The idea was that if all the properties looked a certain way with shared design features, then a village as a whole would look more beautiful. And it worked. 
 这项立法提案本质上是要统一 Berkton 所有房屋的外观审美。其设想是：如果所有房产都按某种方式、带着共同的设计特征呈现，那么整个村庄看起来会更美。而它奏效了。 

 【信号】 提案后紧跟的 "统一外观"＋"奏效了" 。答案信号有两处：一是紧跟提案的目的句 harmonize the aesthetic appearance of all the houses(统一所有房子的外观)，二是收尾的 And it worked.(它奏效了)——"奏效" 确认了这个 "外观统一" 的效果真的实现了，正是提案带来的结果。 

 【替换】 harmonize the aesthetic appearance of all the houses in Berkton ↔ All the houses in Berkton looked aesthetically similar "统一外观"＝"外观看起来相似" 
 shared design features ↔ aesthetically similar "共同设计特征"＝外观相似 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 A 说 designed by the same architect，借用了原文 shared design features 里的 design；但原文说的是 "共同的设计特征"，从没说 "出自同一个建筑师"，A 把 "设计相似" 偷换成 "同一人设计"，是听到 design 就选的陷阱。  借用原文：if all the properties looked a certain way with shared design features 

 B) 偷换概念 B 说 lived in harmony with their neighbours(邻里和睦相处)，疑似借了原文 harmonize(统一)与 an overwhelming majority of neighbors voted 里 neighbors 的影子；但原文是说邻居们 "投票通过提案"，harmonize 指 "统一房屋外观" 而非 "邻里关系和睦"，B 偷换了概念。  借用原文：an overwhelming majority of neighbors voted in favor of "Motion 836" 

 C) 未提及 C 说 enjoyed cosy housing conditions(享受舒适的居住条件)，但原文谈的是房子 "外观是否统一、村子是否更美"，从没谈居民住得舒不舒适；cosy(舒适)是凭 "漂亮房子" 联想出来的，原文无据。

questions.prompt: Why does the man say the tourists are a blessing to Berkton?
options: They have helped boost the local economy.
They have made the residents unusually proud.
They have contributed considerably to its popularity.
They have brought happiness to everyone in the village.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 Why does the man say the tourists are a blessing to Berkton? 

 【翻译】 为什么这位男士说游客是Berkton的福音? 
 A)  他们帮助促进了当地经济。 
 B)  他们使居民感到异常自豪。 
 C)  他们为其知名度做出了相当大的贡献。 
 D)  他们给村里的每个人都带来了快乐。 

 【答案】 A （细节题） They have helped boost the local economy. 
 【定位】 P10 The tourists we receive are a blessing, as they have completely revitalized our local economy. 
 我们接待的游客是一种福气，因为他们彻底重振了我们当地的经济。 

 【信号】 因果词 as 之后即原因 。答案信号是因果连词 as：它前面是判断 The tourists we receive are a blessing，后面 they have completely revitalized our local economy 才是 "为什么是福气" 的真正原因。问 Why，答案就在 as 引出的从句里。 

 【替换】 they have completely revitalized our local economy ↔ They have helped boost the local economy revitalize＝boost，同义替换 

 【排除】 B) 张冠李戴 B 说 made the residents unusually proud，借用了原文前面 Great pride 的 pride；但那是回答 "邻居们现在感受如何" 时说的居民对 "村子变美" 的自豪，不是 "游客" 带来的、也不是 "游客是福气" 的原因，B 张冠李戴、错配了问题。  借用原文：Great pride, I would say. 

 C) 原词陷阱 C 说 contributed considerably to its popularity，借了原文反复出现的 popular/popularity 影子；但说话人给出的 "福气" 原因是 "重振经济"，不是 "游客提升了知名度"，C 把答案换到了名气这条线，与 as 后的原因不符。  借用原文：Berkton has become one of the most popular tourist destinations in the country 

 D) 过度推断 D 说 brought happiness to everyone in the village，疑似从 Every visitor is warmly welcome 的友好氛围里推出来；但原文只说 "重振经济/欢迎游客"，没说 "给村里每个人带来快乐"，everyone/happiness 都是脑补放大，过度推断。  借用原文：Every visitor is warmly welcome.

questions.prompt: What does the passage say about a team of researchers at Northwestern University?
options: They have created the smallest remote-controlled walking robot in the world.
They are going to publish their research findings in the journal Science Robotics.
They are the first to build a robot that can bend, crawl, walk, turn and even jump.
They are engaged in research on a remote-controlled robot which uses special power.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the passage say about a team of researchers at Northwestern University? 

 【翻译】 文章关于Northwestern大学的一组研究人员说了什么？ 
 A)  他们创造了世界上最小的遥控行走机器人。 
 B)  他们将在《Science Robotics》期刊上发表他们的研究成果。 
 C)  他们是第一个制造出能够弯曲、爬行、行走、转弯甚至跳跃的机器人的团队。 
 D)  他们正从事一种使用特殊动力的遥控机器人的研究。 

 【答案】 A （细节题） They have created the smallest remote-controlled walking robot in the world. 
 【定位】 P1 Researchers described it as the smallest-ever remote-controlled walking robot. 
 研究人员把它描述为有史以来最小的遥控步行机器人。 

 【信号】 最高级 smallest-ever 收尾定调 。这句用最高级 the smallest-ever remote-controlled walking robot 给团队成就下定论，最高级是篇章里典型的答案信号，听到 the smallest-ever 就该锁定它为承载结论的那一句。 

 【替换】 the smallest-ever remote-controlled walking robot ↔ the smallest remote-controlled walking robot in the world smallest-ever = smallest…in the world 
 created a remote-controlled robot ↔ They have created 动词 created 直接对应 

 【排除】 B) 原词陷阱 选项B盗用了录音里的期刊名 the journal Science Robotics，但原文只是说"研究发表在该期刊"，并非"将要发表"，更不是问团队的核心成就；它靠你听到 Science Robotics 就想选来设套。  借用原文：In research published in the journal Science Robotics 

 C) 原词陷阱 选项C搬来录音里整串动作 bend, crawl, walk, turn and even jump，极易让人一听就选；但原文从未说该团队是 first to build 会做这些动作的机器人，"第一个"是无中生有，题干问的也是成就定性而非"是否首创动作"。  借用原文：The tiny robot can bend, twist, crawl, walk, turn, and even jump 

 D) 与原文相反 选项D说机器人 uses special power，盗用了录音里的 special power 一词；但原文明说机器人 without the use of complex hardware or special power，是"不用"特殊能源，选项把否定改成了肯定，方向反了。  借用原文：without the use of complex hardware or special power
questions.spoken_text: What does the passage say about a team of researchers at Northwestern University?

questions.prompt: What did the researchers say about the robot they created?
options: It changes its shape by complex hardware.
It is operated by a special type of tiny motor.
It moves from one place to another by memory.
It is powered by the elastic property of its body.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What did the researchers say about the robot they created? 

 【翻译】 研究人员关于他们创造的机器人说了什么？ 
 A)  它通过复杂的硬件改变形状。 
 B)  它由一种特殊类型的微型马达操作。 
 C)  它通过记忆从一个地方移动到另一个地方。 
 D)  它由其身体的弹性特性提供动力。 

 【答案】 D （细节题） It is powered by the elastic property of its body. 
 【定位】 P2 The engineers said this is because the robot is powered by the elastic property of its body. 
 工程师们说，这是因为机器人由其身体的弹性属性提供动力。 

 【信号】 因果 because + powered by 。这句以因果词 because 引出原因，又用 powered by the elastic property of its body 点明供能来源，因果信号 + 原理表述双重锁定它为答案句。 

 【替换】 powered by the elastic property of its body ↔ powered by the elastic property of its body 供能机制几乎原句对应 

 【排除】 A) 与原文相反 选项A说靠 complex hardware 变形，盗用了录音原词 complex hardware；但原文明说机器人做各种动作 without the use of complex hardware，是"不靠"复杂硬件，选项把否定说成了依靠，方向相反。  借用原文：without the use of complex hardware or special power 

 B) 未提及 选项B说靠 a special type of tiny motor 运转，但录音通篇没提任何 motor（马达），供能来源明确是身体弹性；这是凭"机器人=有马达"的常识硬编出来的无中生有项。 
 C) 原词陷阱 选项C把录音里 from one place to another 和 memory（来自 shape-memory）两处原词拼在一起，说机器人 moves…by memory；但原文是靠形状记忆合金"变形再复原"才产生移动，并非"靠记忆移动"，属偷换概念。  借用原文：As the robot deforms and goes back to its original shape, it creates movement from one place to another
questions.spoken_text: What did the researchers say about the robot they created?

questions.prompt: What do the researchers expect their robots to do in the future?
options: Replace humans in exploratory tasks.
Perform tasks in tightly confined spaces.
Explore the structure of clogged arteries.
Assist surgeons in highly complex surgery.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What do the researchers expect their robots to do in the future? 

 【翻译】 研究人员期望他们的机器人未来做什么？ 
 A)  在探索性任务中取代人类。 
 B)  在狭小密闭的空间中执行任务。 
 C)  探索堵塞动脉的结构。 
 D)  在高度复杂的手术中协助外科医生。 

 【答案】 B （细节题） Perform tasks in tightly confined spaces. 
 【定位】 P4 While the research is still in the exploratory phase, the team believes that technology could lead to micro-sized robots that can perform practical tasks in tightly confined spaces. 
 尽管研究仍处于探索阶段，但团队相信，这项技术可能催生出能够在狭小空间内执行实际任务的微型机器人。 

 【信号】 believes + could 引出展望落点 。这句用 the team believes that technology could lead to 表团队对未来的预期，believe + could 是展望性信号，其后 perform practical tasks in tightly confined spaces 就是预期用途的落点。 

 【替换】 perform practical tasks in tightly confined spaces ↔ Perform tasks in tightly confined spaces 执行任务/狭小空间近乎同形 

 【排除】 A) 过度推断 选项A说 Replace humans in exploratory tasks，借了录音里 in the exploratory phase 的 exploratory 一词；但原文只说研究"尚处探索阶段"，从未说要"取代人类"，replace humans 是凭空拔高的过度推断。  借用原文：While the research is still in the exploratory phase 

 C) 原词陷阱 选项C说 Explore the structure of clogged arteries，盗用了录音举例里的 clogged arteries；但 to clear clogged arteries 只是诸多设想用途中的一个例子，且原文是"清理"血管不是"探查结构"，把举例之一冒充成总的未来预期，以偏概全。  借用原文：as surgical assistants to clear clogged arteries 

 D) 原词陷阱 选项D说 Assist surgeons in highly complex surgery，盗用录音 as surgical assistants 的医疗设想；但原文设想的是充当外科助手做清血管/止血等"微创"操作，并未说"辅助高度复杂的手术"，highly complex 是被改大的程度词，同样属举例被偷换。  借用原文：as surgical assistants to clear clogged arteries, to stop internal bleeding, or to eliminate cancerous tumours—all in minimally invasive procedures
questions.spoken_text: What do the researchers expect their robots to do in the future?

questions.prompt: What does the speaker say she did on her ride to the Isles of Scilly?
options: She threw up in the bathroom.
She slept during the entire ride.
She dozed off for a few minutes.
She boasted of her marathon race.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the speaker say she did on her ride to the Isles of Scilly? 

 【翻译】 说话者说她在前往锡利群岛的途中做了什么? 
 A)  她在浴室里呕吐了。 
 B)  她在整个行程中都在睡觉。 
 C)  她打了几分钟瞌睡。 
 D)  她吹嘘自己的马拉松比赛。 

 【答案】 B （细节题） She slept during the entire ride. 
 【定位】 P1 On one very rough ferry crossing, on the route to the Isles of Scilly, for example, my traveling companion spent the entire 3-hour-ride throwing up in the bathroom, while I dozed happily on a plastic chair. 
 比如有一次在去锡利群岛的航线上、那趟非常颠簸的渡轮航程里，我的旅伴整整三个小时都在卫生间呕吐，而我却在一把塑料椅上美美地睡着了。 

 【信号】 对比连词 while 分开「她」和「旅伴」 。while I dozed happily on a plastic chair 里的 while 是答案信号：它把两个人的行为对照开——while 前是旅伴 throwing up in the bathroom，while 后才是「我」做的事。听到 while、whereas 这类对比词，要立刻分清前后各是谁。 

 【替换】 I dozed happily on a plastic chair ↔ She slept during the entire ride. doze 等于睡着，且时长沿用前文 entire 3-hour-ride 

 【排除】 A) 张冠李戴 She threw up in the bathroom. 盗用了录音原词 throwing up in the bathroom，但那是 while 前「我的旅伴」做的事，被安到了「她」头上，典型听到原词就想选的陷阱。  借用原文：my traveling companion spent the entire 3-hour-ride throwing up in the bathroom 

 C) 原词陷阱 She dozed off for a few minutes. 借用了 doze 这个原词，但把时长偷改成「几分钟」，与原文 entire 3-hour-ride 的整程相反，是在「睡多久」上做手脚。  借用原文：I dozed happily on a plastic chair 

 D) 原词陷阱 She boasted of her marathon race. 拼了两个扎眼原词：boast 来自开头 I don't want to boast、marathon 来自 sleep for marathon stretches（指「长时间地睡」，非比赛）。它们都不在「乘船」场景里，且 marathon stretches 根本不是「马拉松比赛」。  借用原文：I will sleep for marathon stretches
questions.spoken_text: What does the speaker say she did on her ride to the Isles of Silly?

questions.prompt: What do we learn from the passage about elite sleepers?
options: They are mostly immune to cognitive impairment.
They can sleep soundly during a rough ride at sea.
They are genetically determined to need less sleep.
They constitute about 13 percent of the population.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What do we learn from the passage about elite sleepers? 

 【翻译】 我们从这段文字中了解到关于精英睡眠者的什么信息? 
 A)  他们大多对认知障碍免疫。 
 B)  他们能在海上颠簸的行程中安然入睡。 
 C)  他们在基因上被决定需要更少的睡眠。 
 D)  他们约占人口的百分之十三。 

 【答案】 C （细节题） They are genetically determined to need less sleep. 
 【定位】 P2 elite sleepers are defined as the approximately 3 percent of the population who are biologically programmed to need less sleep than the rest of us. 
 精英睡眠者被定义为大约占人口3%、在生物学上被设定为比我们其余人需要更少睡眠的那群人。 

 【信号】 下定义句式 are defined as 。elite sleepers are defined as 是答案信号：are defined as 是典型的下定义句式，问某类人特征时，定义句就是答案句。定义里的核心是 biologically programmed to need less sleep。 

 【替换】 biologically programmed to need less sleep ↔ They are genetically determined to need less sleep. biologically programmed 等于 genetically determined 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 They are mostly immune to cognitive impairment. 借了 cognitive 一词（原文 cognitive decline），但原文只说他们少睡时 without any risk of cognitive decline——是「不因少睡而认知衰退」，并非泛泛地「对认知损害免疫」，把条件性表述夸大成绝对免疫。  借用原文：without any risk of cognitive decline 

 B) 张冠李戴 They can sleep soundly during a rough ride at sea. 把第1段讲者本人乘船 very rough ferry crossing 时睡着的事，安到了「精英睡眠者 They」这类人头上，主语张冠李戴；何况第2段恰恰说她其实不是精英睡眠者。  借用原文：On one very rough ferry crossing 

 D) 原词陷阱 They constitute about 13 percent of the population. 盗用了原文的「百分比加人口」结构 approximately 3 percent of the population，却把数字从3%偷改成13%，是典型数字陷阱。  借用原文：the approximately 3 percent of the population
questions.spoken_text: What do we learn from the passage about elite sleepers?

questions.prompt: What has the speaker been trying to find out over the past year?
options: Whether there is a way to reach elite status.
Whether it is possible to modify one's genes.
Whether having a baby impacts one's passion.
Whether one can train themselves to sleep less.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What has the speaker been trying to find out over the past year? 

 【翻译】 说话者在过去一年里一直试图弄清楚什么? 
 A)  是否有办法达到精英睡眠者的状态。 
 B)  是否有可能改变一个人的基因。 
 C)  生孩子是否会影响一个人的热情。 
 D)  一个人是否能训练自己少睡觉。 

 【答案】 D （细节题） Whether one can train themselves to sleep less. 
 【定位】 P3 It may not be possible to change your own genes, but can you train yourself to need less sleep? Is there a non-biological way to reach elite sleeper status? I have spent the past year trying to answer that question. 
 改变自己的基因也许不可能，但你能训练自己变得需要更少睡眠吗？有没有一种非生物学的途径达到精英睡眠者的地位？我过去一年就一直在试图回答这个问题。 

 【信号】 讲者亲口发问加紧跟「我花一年回答这个问题」 。答案信号有二：一是讲者自己抛出的问句 can you train yourself to need less sleep?；二是其后 I have spent the past year trying to answer that question 把「过去一年」与这个问句直接挂钩，明确指认它就是她要弄清的那个问题。 

 【替换】 can you train yourself to need less sleep? ↔ Whether one can train themselves to sleep less. 疑问句改写成 Whether 间接问句，you 变 one 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 Whether there is a way to reach elite status. 借了原文问句里的 reach elite sleeper status，但原文紧接着用 that question 回指的重点是「非生物途径即训练自己少睡」；D 才精确对上她真正探究的内容，A 停在表层措辞。  借用原文：Is there a non-biological way to reach elite sleeper status? 

 B) 与原文相反 Whether it is possible to modify one's genes. 盗用 change your own genes，但原文是 It may not be possible to change your own genes, but——改基因被 but 否定掉、用来引出真正的问题，选它正好取了被推翻的那半句。  借用原文：It may not be possible to change your own genes 

 C) 答非所问 Whether having a baby impacts one's passion. 用了原文的 having a baby 和 a great passion，但原文这两词出现在解释「她为何研究」的背景里，并非她要弄清的那个疑问句，属答非所问。  借用原文：having a baby has severely disrupted my sleep, for which I still have a great passion
questions.spoken_text: What has the speaker been trying to find out over the past year?

questions.prompt: What has the speaker discovered after a year of tough scientific study?
options: It is in fact quite possible to nurture a passion for sleep.
Babies can severely disrupt their parents' sleep patterns.
Being forced to rise early differs from being an early bird.
New parents are forced to jump out of bed at the crack of dawn.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What has the speaker discovered after a year of tough scientific study? 

 【翻译】 说话者在经过一年艰苦的科学研究后发现了什么? 
 A)  事实上完全有可能培养对睡眠的热情。 
 B)  婴儿会严重扰乱父母的睡眠模式。 
 C)  被迫早起不同于成为早起的人。 
 D)  新手父母被迫在破晓时分跳下床。 

 【答案】 C （细节题） Being forced to rise early differs from being an early bird. 
 【定位】 P4 After a year of tough scientific study, however, I have discovered being forced to get up early in the morning is very different from being an early bird. 
 然而，经过一年艰苦的科学研究，我发现被迫早起和真正的早起者是非常不同的两回事。 

 【信号】 转折 however 加标记词 I have discovered 。答案信号有二：however 把前文「我以为我会被迫成为早起者」的旧假设推翻；紧跟的 I have discovered 直接挂出结论。转折后加 discovered 标记的那句就是答案句。 

 【替换】 being forced to get up early in the morning is very different from being an early bird ↔ Being forced to rise early differs from being an early bird. get up early 等于 rise early，is very different from 等于 differs from 

 【排除】 A) 未提及 It is in fact quite possible to nurture a passion for sleep. 拼用了原文的 passion（a great passion），但原文 passion 指「她对睡眠本就有热情」，从未说「可以去培养」，更不是这次研究的发现，属无中生有。  借用原文：for which I still have a great passion 

 B) 原词陷阱 Babies can severely disrupt their parents' sleep patterns. 几乎照搬原文 having a baby has severely disrupted my sleep（disrupt 原词复现），但那是第3段交代的「为什么做研究」，而题问「研究后发现了什么」，时间、逻辑位置都错，答非所问。  借用原文：having a baby has severely disrupted my sleep 

 D) 与原文相反 New parents are forced to jump out of bed at the crack of dawn. 盗用 jump out of bed at the crack of dawn，但原文这是她 I assumed I'd be forced to become 的旧假设，紧接着 however 就把它否定了，取它等于选了被推翻的内容。  借用原文：I assumed I'd be forced to become one of those people who jump out of bed at the crack of dawn
questions.spoken_text: What has the speaker discovered after a year of tough scientific study?

questions.prompt: What does a new paper in the *Quarterly Journal of Experimental Psychology* suggest?
options: We have poor awareness of how many controversial issues are being debated.
No one knows better than yourself what you are thinking about at the moment.
No one can change your opinions more than those who speak in a convincing tone.
We are likely to underestimate how much we can be swayed by a convincing article.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does a new paper in the *Quarterly Journal of Experimental Psychology* suggest? 

 【翻译】 《实验心理学季刊》上的一篇新论文提出了什么? 
 A)  我们对有多少争议性问题正在被讨论缺乏认识。 
 B)  没有人比你自己更清楚此刻你在想什么。 
 C)  没有人能比那些以令人信服的语气说话的人更能改变你的观点。 
 D)  我们可能低估了自己会在多大程度上被一篇有说服力的文章所影响。 

 【答案】 D （细节题） We are likely to underestimate how much we can be swayed by a convincing article. 
 【定位】 P1 And yet a new paper in the Quarterly Journal of Experimental Psychology suggests that we actually have very poor awareness of our own belief change, meaning that we will tend to underestimate how much we've been swayed by a convincing article. 
 然而，《实验心理学季刊》上的一篇新论文表明，我们其实对自己信念的变化觉察得很差，这意味着我们往往会低估自己被一篇有说服力的文章左右的程度。 

 【信号】 转折 And yet 后才是真意 。前一句说"没人比你更了解自己的想法，你似乎该知道信念变没变"，紧接一个转折 And yet，研究真正的结论在转折之后；听到 And yet 就该锁定其后这句为答案句，而非顺着前面那句"你最懂自己"去选。 

 【替换】 we will tend to underestimate how much we've been swayed by a convincing article ↔ We are likely to underestimate how much we can be swayed by a convincing article. 近乎同义改写、只换情态词 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 选项说我们对"有多少争议话题正在被讨论"觉察很差，盗用了录音 very poor awareness 这个原词，但录音说的是对"自己信念变化"觉察差，A 把觉察的对象偷换成了"有多少争议话题"，答非所问。  借用原文：we actually have very poor awareness of our own belief change 

 B) 与原文相反 选项"没人比你更了解你此刻在想什么"几乎照搬录音开头 No one knows your own mind like you do，但那是作者先立的"看似如此"的常识、随即被 And yet 推翻，并非论文的 suggest（结论），拿被推翻的铺垫当答案。  借用原文：No one knows your own mind like you do 

 C) 偷换概念 选项说"用有说服力语气说话的人最能改变你的看法"，蹭了录音 a convincing article 里 convincing 一词，却把"有说服力的文章"换成了"有说服力的语气（tone）"，且"没人比这更能改变你看法"录音从未说，属偷换加无中生有。  借用原文：swayed by a convincing article
questions.spoken_text: What does a new paper in the Quarterly Journal of Experimental Psychology suggest?

questions.prompt: What happened when the students read a text that argued against their own initial position?
options: Their belief about physical punishment changed.
Their memory pushed them toward a current belief.
The memory of their initial belief came back to them.
Their experiences of physical punishment haunted them.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What happened when the students read a text that argued against their own initial position? 

 【翻译】 当学生们阅读一篇反对他们自己最初立场的文章时发生了什么? 
 A)  他们对体罚的看法改变了。 
 B)  他们的记忆将他们推向了当前的信念。 
 C)  他们对最初信念的记忆回到了他们脑海中。 
 D)  他们遭受体罚的经历困扰着他们。 

 【答案】 A （细节题） Their belief about physical punishment changed. 
 【定位】 P3 The students' belief about physical punishment changed when they read a text that argued against their own initial position. 
 当学生读到一篇与自己最初立场相反的文章时，他们对体罚的信念发生了改变。 

 【信号】 题干条件原话复现处即答案句 。录音 when they read a text that argued against their own initial position 与题干条件几乎一字不差，这种"题干条件在录音里原话出现"的位置，紧挨着的主句就是答案句；本句主句正是 The students' belief about physical punishment changed。 

 【替换】 The students' belief about physical punishment changed ↔ Their belief about physical punishment changed. 几乎原句对应、仅换主语为代词 

 【排除】 B) 答非所问 选项"他们的记忆把他们推向当前信念"蹭了录音 the memory of their initial belief was shifted in the direction of their new belief，但那是"信念已改变"之后另起的现象（记忆偏移），不是题干问的"读到反对文章时直接发生了什么"；记忆偏移是次级结果，答非所问。  借用原文：the memory of their initial belief was shifted in the direction of their new belief 

 C) 与原文相反 选项说"他们最初信念的记忆回来了（came back）"，但录音明确说记忆 was shifted in the direction of their new belief、closer to their current belief than their original belief，即对原信念的记忆被改写、偏离了，而非"回来了"，方向恰好相反。  借用原文：their memory was closer to their current belief than their original belief 

 D) 未提及 选项说"他们受体罚的亲身经历困扰着他们"，录音通篇只讲对体罚"是否有效"的信念与记忆，从未提学生本人"受过体罚的经历（experiences of physical punishment）"，更没说被 haunted（困扰），属凭 physical punishment 这个话题词臆造。
questions.spoken_text: What happened when the students read a text that argued against their own initial position?

questions.prompt: What did the researchers concede concerning their findings?
options: They apparently have little to do with moderate beliefs.
They don't reflect the change of view on physical punishment.
They may not apply to changes to extreme or deeply held beliefs.
They are unlikely to alter people's position without more evidence.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What did the researchers concede concerning their findings? 

 【翻译】 研究人员承认他们的研究结果存在什么问题? 
 A)  这些结果显然与温和的信念关系不大。 
 B)  这些结果没有反映出对体罚看法的变化。 
 C)  这些结果可能不适用于极端或根深蒂固的信念的改变。 
 D)  如果没有更多证据,这些结果不太可能改变人们的立场。 

 【答案】 C （细节题） They may not apply to changes to extreme or deeply held beliefs. 
 【定位】 P4 The researchers concede that this research was about changes to mostly moderate beliefs—it's likely the findings would be different in the context of changes to extreme or deeply held beliefs. 
 研究者承认，这项研究针对的大多是温和信念的变化——很可能在极端或根深蒂固的信念发生变化时，研究结论会有所不同。 

 【信号】 concede 后的让步句即答案 。题干里的 concede 在录音 The researchers concede that 原词出现，其后破折号引出的 it's likely the findings would be different in the context of changes to extreme or deeply held beliefs 就是研究者承认的局限，正是答案句。 

 【替换】 it's likely the findings would be different in the context of changes to extreme or deeply held beliefs ↔ They may not apply to changes to extreme or deeply held beliefs. "结论会不同"="可能不适用" 

 【排除】 A) 与原文相反 选项说结论"与温和信念几乎无关（little to do with moderate beliefs）"，蹭了录音 mostly moderate beliefs，但录音恰恰说这项研究就是"关于温和信念"的，结论正适用于温和信念，A 把适用对象说成了无关，与原文相反。  借用原文：this research was about changes to mostly moderate beliefs 

 B) 未提及 选项说研究结论"没有反映对体罚看法的变化"，但录音第三段恰恰证明了看法会变（The students' belief about physical punishment changed），研究者承认的是"对极端信念可能不适用"，从没说"没反映看法变化"，属臆造。 
 D) 过度推断 选项说"没有更多证据，结论难以改变人们立场"，听感上像研究的谨慎口吻，但录音研究者承认的是适用范围（极端信念可能不适用），从未提"需要更多证据才能改变立场"，evidence 的说法是凭学术语感臆造的。

questions.prompt: What does the speaker conclude from her analysis of the Census Bureau's data?
options: American moms have been increasingly inclined to live alone.
The American population has been on the rise in the past 25 years.
American motherhood has actually been on the decline.
The fertility rates in America have in fact been falling sharply.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the speaker conclude from her analysis of the Census Bureau's data? 

 【翻译】 说话者从她对人口普查局数据的分析中得出了什么结论? 
 A)  美国母亲越来越倾向于独自生活。 
 B)  过去25年美国人口一直在增长。 
 C)  美国母亲身份实际上一直在减少。 
 D)  美国的生育率实际上一直在急剧下降。 

 【答案】 C （细节题） American motherhood has actually been on the decline. 
 【定位】 P2 According to my analysis of data from the Census Bureau, the decline of American motherhood is real, occurring very quickly, and may continue for some time yet. 
 根据我对普查局数据的分析，美国 "当母亲" 这件事的减少是真实存在的，正在迅速发生，而且可能还会持续一段时间。 

 【信号】 题干原话回扣 + 断言语气 "is real" 。这句以 According to my analysis of data from the Census Bureau 直接回扣题干的 "analysis of the Census Bureau's data"，紧接着用断言语气 the decline of American motherhood is real，"is real（确实如此）" 这种作者明确下判断的口吻就是结论信号。 

 【替换】 the decline of American motherhood is real ↔ American motherhood has actually been on the decline 名词/动词换说法，意思同为 "母亲减少" 

 【排除】 A) 未提及 American moms have been increasingly inclined to live alone 说母亲越来越爱独居，全文谈的是母亲数量/比例下降，从未提母亲的居住方式，属凭空添加的内容。 
 B) 原词陷阱 The American population has been on the rise 借用了原文 As the American population grows 的原词，人口确实在涨，但题干问的是作者从数据得出的 "结论"，作者的结论是母亲在减少，人口上涨只是铺垫前提，不是结论本身。  借用原文：As the American population grows 

 D) 原词陷阱 The fertility rates in America have in fact been falling sharply 用了原文 fertility rates are falling sharply 的原词，可作者的结论对象是 "motherhood（当母亲）" 而非 "fertility rates（生育率）"——原文里生育率下降是 "frequently noted（常被提到）" 的旧事，作者要讲的 "less-observed（少被注意）" 的新结论是母亲减少。  借用原文：fertility rates are falling sharply
questions.spoken_text: What does the speaker conclude from her analysis of the Census Bureau's data?

questions.prompt: What does the speaker say is a positive consequence of the age shift in childbearing?
options: More new mothers tend to take greater care of their children.
More new mothers are economically able to raise children.
A larger proportion of women take pride in their children.
A larger proportion of women really enjoy motherhood.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the speaker say is a positive consequence of the age shift in childbearing? 

 【翻译】 说话者认为生育年龄推移带来的积极后果是什么? 
 A)  更多新手母亲倾向于更悉心照顾她们的孩子。 
 B)  更多新手母亲在经济上有能力抚养孩子。 
 C)  更大比例的女性为她们的孩子感到自豪。 
 D)  更大比例的女性真正享受母亲身份。 

 【答案】 B （细节题） More new mothers are economically able to raise children. 
 【定位】 P5 One positive consequence of this age shift is that a larger proportion of new mothers are economically prepared to raise children. 
 这一年龄变化带来的一个正面后果是：更大比例的新晋母亲在经济上已为养育孩子做好了准备。 

 【信号】 作者亲口贴的 "positive consequence" 标签 。这句开头 One positive consequence of this age shift is that 与题干用词几乎一字不差，"positive consequence" 是作者明确贴上的 "好处" 标签，标签之后的内容就是要找的答案句。 

 【替换】 a larger proportion of new mothers are economically prepared to raise children ↔ More new mothers are economically able to raise children "economically prepared"≈"economically able"，比例≈more 

 【排除】 A) 未提及 More new mothers tend to take greater care of their children 说更多新母亲更用心照顾孩子，原文讲的好处是 "经济上准备好"，从没说她们更会/更用心照顾，属凭空添加。 
 C) 原词陷阱 A larger proportion of women take pride in their children 借用了原文 a larger proportion 的原词造出熟悉感，但作者说的是 "economically prepared"，根本没提 "take pride（自豪）"，比例的对象被悄悄换成了情感。  借用原文：a larger proportion of new mothers 

 D) 原词陷阱 A larger proportion of women really enjoy motherhood 说更大比例女性享受当母亲，同样套用了 "a larger proportion" 的措辞，但原文的好处是经济准备，没说享受，且全文末句 later motherhood means less motherhood 的基调也不是在讲享受。  借用原文：a larger proportion of new mothers
questions.spoken_text: What does the speaker say is a positive consequence of the age shift in childbearing?

questions.prompt: What might be one explanation for the rise in retail spending on Mother's Day?
options: The meaning of motherhood has changed considerably.
More and more mothers go shopping to treat themselves.
More mothers have adult children celebrating the holiday.
The number of American mothers has been growing steadily.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What might be one explanation for the rise in retail spending on Mother's Day? 

 【翻译】 母亲节零售消费增长的一个可能解释是什么? 
 A)  母亲身份的含义已经发生了相当大的变化。 
 B)  越来越多的母亲去购物犒劳自己。 
 C)  更多母亲有成年子女庆祝这个节日。 
 D)  美国母亲的数量一直在稳步增长。 

 【答案】 C （细节题） More mothers have adult children celebrating the holiday. 
 【定位】 P6 It is hard to say if Mother's Day spending is rising more than one would expect ... but one factor might be that the proportion of women who are the mothers of adult children is rising. And those adult children may spend more generously when it comes to celebrating the moms they no longer live with. 
 很难说母亲节开销是否涨得超出预期……但一个因素可能是：身为成年子女之母亲的女性占比在上升。而这些成年子女在为已不同住的母亲庆祝时，可能花钱更大方。 

 【信号】 给原因的标记 "one factor might be" 。这句用 one factor might be that 明确引出原因，与题干 "one explanation" 对应；后一句 those adult children may spend more generously 进一步点明是成年子女花钱多，原因信号清晰。 

 【替换】 those adult children may spend more generously when it comes to celebrating the moms ↔ More mothers have adult children celebrating the holiday 因果同一件事换主语视角表述 

 【排除】 A) 过度推断 The meaning of motherhood has changed considerably 说母亲节/母亲身份的含义大变，原文只说开销上涨的一个具体原因是成年子女花钱，并未上升到 "含义改变" 这种概括判断，属过度拔高。 
 B) 张冠李戴 More and more mothers go shopping to treat themselves 借了原文 "spend/spending" 的花钱语境，但原文是 those adult children may spend more generously——掏钱的是成年子女，不是母亲自己购物犒劳自己，主体张冠李戴。  借用原文：those adult children may spend more generously 

 D) 与原文相反 The number of American mothers has been growing steadily 说母亲数量稳步增长，这与全文结论 the decline of American motherhood is real 正好相反；况且作者还专门指出 given that the American population keeps growing 的是人口、不是母亲，选项把对象与方向都弄反了。  借用原文：given that the American population keeps growing
questions.spoken_text: What might be one explanation for the rise in retail spending on Mother's Day?

questions.prompt: What does NASA's 1989 paper claim houseplants can do?
options: A) Add to indoor toxic pollutants.
Absorb poisonous chemicals.
Beautify the home environment.
Soak up surrounding moisture.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does NASA's 1989 paper claim houseplants can do? 

 【翻译】 NASA 1989年的论文声称室内植物能做什么? 
 A)  增加室内有毒污染物。 
 B)  吸收有毒化学物质。 
 C)  美化家居环境。 
 D)  吸收周围湿气。 

 【答案】 B （细节题） Absorb poisonous chemicals. 
 【定位】 P1 Since NASA published a paper in 1989 claiming that houseplants can soak up pollution and toxic chemicals, businesses and homeowners have increasingly invested in greenery to help clean their air. 
 自从 NASA 于 1989 年发表一篇论文，宣称室内植物能吸走污染和有毒化学物质以来，企业和房主便越来越多地投资绿植来帮助净化空气。 

 【信号】 claiming 后接论文主张 。录音开头 claiming that houseplants can soak up pollution and toxic chemicals 中的 claiming 直接对应题干的 claim，是论文主张的落点，紧跟其后的内容就是答案句。 

 【替换】 soak up pollution and toxic chemicals ↔ Absorb poisonous chemicals. soak up=Absorb，toxic=poisonous 

 【排除】 A) 与原文相反 Add to indoor toxic pollutants. 盗用了录音里的 toxic chemicals（有毒化学物）一词，却把『吸走』反说成『增加』，与论文主张正好相反。  借用原文：houseplants can soak up pollution and toxic chemicals 

 C) 未提及 Beautify the home environment. 是植物『好看』的生活常识，录音从头到尾只谈净化空气、从未提美化，属凭常识硬填。 
 D) 原词陷阱 Soak up surrounding moisture. 借用了答案句 soak up 这个动词，却把吸收对象从『污染物』偷换成『水分（moisture）』，录音并未说植物吸潮。  借用原文：houseplants can soak up pollution and toxic chemicals
questions.spoken_text: What does NASA's 1989 paper claim houseplants can do?

questions.prompt: What is said to be the problem with NASA's study reported in its 1989 paper?
options: NASA did experiments in sealed containers resembling the super insulated offices of 1970s.
It was based on experiments under conditions unlike those in most homes or offices.
NASA conducted tests in outer space whose environment is different from ours.
It drew its conclusion without any contrastive data from other experiments.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What is said to be the problem with NASA's study reported in its 1989 paper? 

 【翻译】 NASA 1989年论文中报告的研究存在什么问题? 
 A)  NASA在类似1970年代超级隔热办公室的密封容器中进行了实验。 
 B)  该研究基于与大多数家庭或办公室条件不同的实验。 
 C)  NASA在外太空进行了测试,其环境与我们的环境不同。 
 D)  该研究在没有其他实验对比数据的情况下得出了结论。 

 【答案】 B （细节题） It was based on experiments under conditions unlike those in most homes or offices. 
 【定位】 P2 The problem lies in the fact that NASA conducted their tests in sealed containers that do not simulate the conditions in most people's homes or offices. 
 问题在于，NASA 是在密封容器里做的实验，而这种容器并不能模拟大多数人家里或办公室的环境。 

 【信号】 The problem lies in 明示缺陷 。The problem lies in the fact that 是直接点题的标志，问题就在这句之后——这正是题干 the problem 的对应落点。 

 【替换】 sealed containers that do not simulate the conditions in most people's homes or offices ↔ It was based on experiments under conditions unlike those in most homes or offices. do not simulate=unlike 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 NASA did experiments in sealed containers resembling the super insulated offices of 1970s. 把录音真出现的 sealed containers 和 super insulated 两处原词硬拼，还说密封舱『像 1970 年代办公室』——录音说密封舱『不模拟』普通环境，二者恰恰不像，属张冠李戴式拼接。  借用原文：sealed containers that do not simulate the conditions 

 C) 过度推断 NASA conducted tests in outer space whose environment is different from ours. 借了录音 space stations 的太空联想，但录音说实验是在 sealed containers 里做的，从没说在 outer space 做测试，属无中生有。  借用原文：keeping the air fresh for astronauts cut off in biospheres or space stations 

 D) 未提及 It drew its conclusion without any contrastive data from other experiments. 说该研究『缺对照数据』，录音指出的缺陷是『实验条件不真实』，从未提缺对照数据，属未提及。
questions.spoken_text: What is said to be the problem with NASA's study reported in its 1989 paper?

questions.prompt: What is the finding of a new evaluation of dozens of studies spanning 30 years?
options: Natural ventilation proves much more efficient for cleaning the air than houseplants.
Houseplants disperse chemical compounds more quickly with people moving around.
Natural ventilation turns out to be most effective with doors and windows wide open.
Houseplants in a normal environment rarely have any adverse impact on the air.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What is the finding of a new evaluation of dozens of studies spanning 30 years? 

 【翻译】 对跨越30年的数十项研究进行的新评估有何发现? 
 A)  自然通风在清洁空气方面比室内植物有效得多。 
 B)  随着人员走动,室内植物更快地散发化学化合物。 
 C)  自然通风在门窗大开时最为有效。 
 D)  正常环境中的室内植物很少对空气产生任何不良影响。 

 【答案】 A （细节题） Natural ventilation proves much more efficient for cleaning the air than houseplants. 
 【定位】 P3 However, a new evaluation of dozens of studies spanning 30 years found that houseplants in a normal environment have little impact. In fact, natural ventilation is far better at cleaning the air. 
 然而，一项跨越 30 年、对数十项研究的新评估发现，正常环境下的室内植物作用甚微。事实上，自然通风在净化空气方面要好得多。 

 【信号】 However 转折后是真结论 。However, a new evaluation 用 However 把语气从『植物有用』扭向新结论，转折之后的两句才是答案落点，尤其 In fact, natural ventilation is far better 是核心。 

 【替换】 natural ventilation is far better at cleaning the air ↔ Natural ventilation proves much more efficient for cleaning the air than houseplants. far better=much more efficient 

 【排除】 B) 原词陷阱 Houseplants disperse chemical compounds more quickly with people moving around. 盗用了录音 disperse the compounds 和 movement of people 两处原词，却说『植物因人走动散得更快』；录音的意思是建筑本身的换气率（人来人往开门窗）远高于植物的散播率，是在贬低植物，而非夸植物散得快，方向被偷换。  借用原文：the rate at which plants disperse the compounds was well below the usual rate of air exchange 

 C) 过度推断 Natural ventilation turns out to be most effective with doors and windows wide open. 借了录音 opening doors and windows 的原词，却加上『most effective / wide open』这种录音没说的最高级和条件；录音只说通风比植物好，没说门窗全开才最有效。  借用原文：opening doors and windows 

 D) 偷换概念 Houseplants in a normal environment rarely have any adverse impact on the air. 几乎照搬了录音 houseplants in a normal environment have little impact，但把 little impact（作用甚微）偷换成 rarely have any adverse impact（几乎无害）——录音说的是植物『没多大净化作用』，不是说植物『无害』，含义跑偏。  借用原文：houseplants in a normal environment have little impact

questions.prompt: What does NASA's sealed experiment recommendation exemplify in scientists' pursuit of truth?
options: The root cause for misinterpretations of scientific findings.
The difficulty in understanding what's actually happening.
The steps to be taken in arriving at any conclusion with certainty.
The necessity of continually reexamining and challenging findings.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does NASA's sealed experiment recommendation exemplify in scientists' pursuit of truth? 

 【翻译】 NASA的密封实验建议在科学家追求真理的过程中体现了什么? 
 A)  科学发现被误读的根本原因。 
 B)  理解实际发生情况的难度。 
 C)  确定无疑地得出任何结论所需采取的步骤。 
 D)  不断重新审查和质疑研究发现的必要性。 

 【答案】 D （推断题） The necessity of continually reexamining and challenging findings. 
 【定位】 P5 This is certainly an example of how scientific findings can be misleading or misinterpreted over time. But it's also a great example of how scientific research should continually reexamine and question findings to get closer to the ground truth of understanding what's actually happening. 
 这无疑是一个例子，说明科学发现如何会随时间被误导或误读。但它也是一个绝佳的例子，说明科学研究应当不断重新审视、质疑已有结论，以更接近事情真相的理解。 

 【信号】 But also 转向真正落点 。结尾两句用 But it's also a great example of 把重点从『发现会被误读』转到『科研应不断重审质疑』；题干问 pursuit of truth（追求真理），对应的正是 But 之后这句升华。 

 【替换】 scientific research should continually reexamine and question findings ↔ The necessity of continually reexamining and challenging findings. should=necessity，question=challenging 

 【排除】 A) 与原文相反 The root cause for misinterpretations of scientific findings. 抓的是 But 之前那句 can be misleading or misinterpreted，且录音只说会被误读、从未分析『根本原因（root cause）』，既取错重心又无中生有。  借用原文：how scientific findings can be misleading or misinterpreted over time 

 B) 原词陷阱 The difficulty in understanding what's actually happening. 盗用了录音结尾 understanding what's actually happening 这串原词，却把它说成『理解之难（difficulty）』；录音说的是科研应不断质疑以『接近』真相，重点是方法而非『难』，属截取原词答非所问。  借用原文：to get closer to the ground truth of understanding what's actually happening 

 C) 未提及 The steps to be taken in arriving at any conclusion with certainty. 说『下确定结论的步骤』，录音强调的恰恰是『不断重审质疑、逼近真相』这种开放过程，并未给出『确定结论的步骤』，且 certainty 与录音口吻相反，属未提及兼相反。
questions.spoken_text: What does NASA's sealed experiment recommendation exemplify in scientists' pursuit of truth?
